events.title: Born on Zakynthos
events.description: Niccolò Foscolo is born on the island of Zakynthos, then part of the Republic of Venice, to Andrea Foscolo, a Venetian physician, and Diamantina Spathis, who is Greek. He will later take the name Ugo.

events.title: His father dies
events.description: After the early death of his father, the family’s finances collapse. Foscolo, who had begun his studies in the seminary of Spalato, goes back to Zakynthos with his mother’s family.

events.title: Moves to Venice
events.description: His mother settles in Venice and Foscolo joins her. He studies and becomes involved in the literary and political life of the city.

events.title: Tieste staged in Venice
events.description: His tragedy Tieste is performed in Venice, one of his first public successes.

events.title: Treaty of Campoformio
events.description: Napoleon cedes Venice to Austria. Disillusioned, Foscolo leaves the city for Milan. The same disillusion is the background of Jacopo Ortis, who flees Venice to the Euganean Hills.

events.title: Ortis, Bologna edition
events.description: The first printed edition of the Ortis comes out in Bologna, printed by Marsigli. Foscolo, who had left Bologna, later disowned it.

events.title: Vera storia di due amanti infelici
events.description: [To be completed] Edition of the Ortis known by the title Vera storia di due amanti infelici.

events.title: Milan edition (Goethe’s copy)
events.description: [To be completed] Milan edition of 1801, in the copy that belonged to Goethe.

events.title: Ortis, Milan edition (Genio Tipografico)
events.description: The Milan edition of 1802. In the editor’s notice, the editor disowns the earlier editions, printed in Bologna and Turin, and says that only this one is authentic.

events.title: Service in France
events.description: Foscolo serves with the Italian troops sent to France for the planned invasion of England. In these years he has a daughter, Floriana, with the Englishwoman Mary (Fanny) Hamilton. In 1806 he returns to Italy.

events.title: Dei Sepolcri
events.description: The poem Dei Sepolcri establishes his reputation as a poet.

events.title: Chair of eloquence at Pavia
events.description: Foscolo is appointed to the chair of Italian eloquence at the University of Pavia and gives his inaugural lecture in 1809. The chair is abolished within months.

events.title: Flight from Milan
events.description: To avoid taking the oath of allegiance to the Austrian emperor, Foscolo leaves Milan. After a few weeks in Switzerland he settles in Zurich and Hottingen at the end of May.

events.title: Ortis, Zurich edition
events.description: The third edition of the Ortis is published in Switzerland by the publisher Füssli of Zurich, with additions written in exile.

events.title: Arrival in London
events.description: Foscolo leaves Zurich on 27 July 1816 and, after a stop in Basel, reaches London, where he is welcomed by liberal circles and by the Italian exiles.

events.title: Ortis, London edition (Murray)
events.description: The Ortis is printed in London by the publisher John Murray, in two volumes.

events.title: Dies at Turnham Green
events.description: Foscolo dies of dropsy at Turnham Green, near London, and is buried there.

events.title: Remains moved to Santa Croce
events.description: His remains are brought to Florence and placed in the Basilica of Santa Croce, among the great Italians.
